title.en: Checking a proof is a computation

t.en: The second step: proofs become numbers too. A proof is a tree whose leaves are axioms and whose forks are each an Apply, as wired on the board; a tree can be coded as a number. Checking a proof looks at two things: every leaf is in the table of axioms, and every Apply fits (the “if A then B” meets just A). The table holds: it rains, it rains → the ground is wet, the ground is wet → the road is slippery.

after.en: “A can be proved” thus becomes a sentence about numbers: some number is a proof that passes the check and concludes A. It is written Prov(⌜A⌝).

stated: ok(use(x, y)) = both(both(ok(x), ok(y)), fits(concl(x), concl(y)))

tests.goal: ok(use(ax(imp(wet, slip)), use(ax(imp(rain, wet)), ax(rain)))) = tt
concl(use(ax(imp(wet, slip)), use(ax(imp(rain, wet)), ax(rain)))) = slip

brief.en: Design a proof assistant that proves every goal.
